h_title: Business transformation leader for SAP S/4HANA programs
h_sub: I help enterprises simplify their operating model and deploy global templates that scale, and put AI to practical use.
d_1: Fewer than one in five organizations redesign their processes when they move to S/4HANA, while 49% do little or no re-engineering. Yet nearly 60% of these programs still finish behind schedule and over budget.
d_2: Choosing the conservative path to protect schedule and budget does not appear to protect either: most programs overrun anyway, driven by underestimated complexity, growing scope and limited internal capacity, none of which a like-for-like move removes.
d_2b: The bigger cost arrives later, because the processes and data you carry over set the ceiling for the automation and AI use cases you can deploy after go-live.
d_2c: For every organization that redesigns, far more preserve (49% versus fewer than 20%), so the "safe" choice is also the crowded one.
d_3: When you look at the processes you plan to carry over, which ones would you still want to be running unchanged once automation and AI are part of daily operations?
d_src: Source: ISG, State of SAP Migrations, February 2026 (survey of 200+ senior decision-makers).
a_1: Business transformation leader with extensive experience delivering large-scale SAP S/4HANA programs. My core expertise is enterprise transformation, operating model simplification and global template deployment, across Quote-to-Cash, Supply Chain and intercompany models.
a_2: I focus on the practical application of Business AI to reshape enterprise operations, automate complex processes and accelerate value realization.
a_3: Outside of work, I am a mountain enthusiast: climbing and ski touring across the Mont-Blanc massif, the Valais, the Bernese Oberland and the Vanoise.
